page: OVHcloud l4-90 is a GPU-accelerated server instance within the Cloud GPU family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 22 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9454 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.75 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 90.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 4.09 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance is equipped with a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data highlights strong computational capabilities, particularly in single-core and specialized workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while multi-core performance is strong (top 25%). The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), which contribute to its strong performance in Passmark CPU extended instructions and physics tests. In memory benchmarks, the instance achieves a strong Passmark memory score, though large-block memory bandwidth read and write speeds remain in the average tier.

The integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for small and medium language model inference. For a 135M parameter model, prompt processing reaches 12,364.91 tokens per second, and text generation achieves 511.95 tokens per second. For a medium 7B parameter model, prompt processing operates at 2,286.1 tokens per second and generation at 54.36 tokens per second, both placing in the top 10% tier. Large 70B model prompt processing remains strong at 35.65 tokens per second, though text generation data is unavailable for this model size.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the l4-90 offers a balanced resource density by pairing dedicated AMD EPYC CPU cores with a modern Ada Lovelace GPU and local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the higher overhead of multi-GPU systems while delivering top-tier inference speeds for small-to-medium models. The server is highly suited for workloads such as machine learning inference, image processing, physical simulations, and compute-heavy applications requiring dedicated CPU resources and hardware acceleration.
